"...until you have paid," <note>original Greek: *apodōs*</note> says Luke. However, it is most certain that the sinner is unable to pay, both from Matthew 18:25 and from the "analogy of faith" <note>the theological principle that any interpretation of a specific Bible verse must be consistent with the core truths of the faith</note>, due to humanity’s total inability to save itself and the fact that continued sin deserves punishment into all eternity.

XXIII. Nor can the strength of this argument be broken by the **"invention of a middle-ground,"** <note>original: *figmento temperamenti*</note> by which the sinner would pay in part through his own person, while that which remained to be paid would be wiped away through the grace of God and the **merit of Christ**. For both the text itself—which commands the debtor to pay the *last penny* <note>original Latin: *ultimum obolum*; a reference to the smallest denomination of coin used to symbolize a complete debt</note>—and the following passages confirm the opposite, as they completely overturn this middle-ground and forbid any mixing of Christ's merit with one's own satisfaction for sin. We assign the fifth category to those sayings that destroy the hope not only of Redemption but also of all the means toward Redemption in the future life. For Redemption to be granted, both the **Forgiveness of sins** and **Effective Conversion** are required. Sacred Scripture teaches us that both are sought in vain in eternity.

XXIV. It is evident from Matthew 12:32 that the hope for the **Forgiveness of sins** expires with the end of this life: *Whoever speaks a word against the **Holy Spirit** will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the age to come.* Whether "this age and the one to come" is understood as the **Dispensations of the Old and New Testament** <note>original: *Oeconomia*; the historical systems of God’s dealings with humanity</note> (as **Teelmann** <note>Henricus Teelmann (1694–1764), a Dutch Reformed theologian known for his "Sacred Exercises"</note> argues in his *Sacred Exercises*, p. 112 ff.), or as the present and future life (as the vast majority of interpreters <note>original: *interpretum integra inclinat sylva*; literally, "the whole forest of interpreters leans this way"</note> suggest), it is clear from Jewish usage that it signifies "never." This is also confirmed by Mark 3:29, which says: *he has no forgiveness forever, but is subject to eternal judgment.* <note>original Greek: *ouk echei aphesin eis ton aiōna, all’ enochos estin aiōniou krimatos*</note> Now, that phrase "forever" <note>original Greek: *eis ton aiōna*</note> is constantly used by the Savior and the New Testament writers to mean an eternity that never ends. Furthermore, our theologians have shown abundantly that even the defenders of **Purgatory** gain nothing from this saying. It is even more opposed to the defenders of absolute **Universal Restoration** <note>original Greek: *Apokatastaseōs*; the theological theory that all beings, including the damned and the devil, will eventually be reconciled to God</note>, especially when we embrace the simplest sense of the words. <summary>This page argues against the possibility of escaping eternal punishment through partial payment or divine grace after death. It uses Matthew 12:32 to demonstrate that forgiveness for certain sins is impossible in the future life, refuting the concepts of Purgatory and Universal Restoration.</summary>

The time, when Eucritus and I were walking toward the Hales
From the city; and Amyntas was with us as the third.
For Phrasidamus and Antigenes, the two sons of Lycopeus, were celebrating the harvest festival <note>original: "Thalysia"</note>
And they offered up something of their wealth from above, from the line of Clytia and the very
Chalkon, who struck a spring from the ground with his foot.
He set his knee firmly upon the rock; and there beside it,
Poplars and elm trees showed a shady grove;
Overarched and thick with green leaves.
And we had not yet finished half the road; nor had the tomb
Of Brasilas appeared to us, when we found a certain traveler,
A noble man skilled in the Muses, a Cydonian.
His name was Lycidas; and he was a goatherd; nor would anyone
Have failed to recognize him upon seeing him; for he looked exactly like a goatherd.
For he wore the tawny skin of a shaggy goat upon his shoulders,
Smelling of fresh rennet.
And an old tunic was fastened around his chest
With a woven belt; and in his right hand he held a curved staff of wild olive,
And he spoke to me quietly, his face
Wearing a smiling look; and a laugh clung to his lip.
Simichidas, where do you drag your feet at high noon,
When even the lizard sleeps upon the stone walls?

### of the Kingdom of Chile.

tain throughout the entire country, by means of their natural vehicles, the air and the water, are likely the cause of the constant fertility that learned observers admire there. Even the internal heat, originating from the many minerals capable of maintaining it—with which all that land is impregnated—may likewise contribute to this productive power. With these natural aids, the soil can perform very well without the external use of fertilizers <note>original: "abonos".</note>. 

This is the belief of farmers seasoned by experience, who judge the adoption of such methods as harmful, or at least superfluous for their fields. As proof, they cite the unalterable fecundity of the lands surrounding the Capital <note>Santiago de Chile, the administrative center of the colony.</note>. These fields were sown annually by the ancient Indians <note>Molina refers here to the indigenous Picunche people of the central valley.</note>, who were numerous in that region, and have since been cultivated by the Spaniards for a period of 239 years. Without the reinforcement or aid of fertilizers or artificial manures <note>original: "engrasos artificiales"; the author suggests that the natural mineral composition of the earth is superior to traditional animal waste.</note>, these lands have not yet shown the slightest sign of exhaustion or decline, neither in the quantity nor the quality of their harvest. It is perhaps because of this lack of manure that Chilean soil is not infested with the worms that destroy budding plants; such pests likely multiply much more than they should through the fermentation and putrefaction of dung.

### Alchemical Questions, Question 73

...beings, he acknowledges a twofold heat: one that is active and formal, which mixes the **elementary** <note>the four basic building blocks: earth, air, fire, and water</note> qualities in various ways. This heat is not merely an analogy based on its divine effects, but is celestial in its very origin and essence. Nevertheless, within this elementary world, it becomes "elementary" in a certain manner. For just as the elements exist within the stars—as heat exists in the Sun and Mars, and cold in the celestial Saturn—in a celestial way; and just as all things exist in God preeminently; so too do celestial things exist within the elements in an elementary way. **Aristotle** agrees in the third book of *On the Generation of Animals*, in the final chapter:

> <note>original Greek: γίνεται δ’ ἐν γῆ καὶ ὑγρῷ τὰ ζῶα καὶ τὰ φυτὰ, διὰ τὸ ἐν γῆ μὲν ὑπάρχειν ὑγρὸν, ἐν δ’ ὕδατι πνεῦμα, ἐν δὲ τῷ παντὶ θερμότητα ψυχικὴν.</note> 
> Animals and plants are formed in the earth and in moisture, because moisture exists in the earth, and **spirit** <note>original Greek: *pneuma*; a life-giving breath or subtle essence</note> exists in water, and in the whole of the universe there is a **soul-heat** <note>original Greek: *thermotēta psychikēn*; literally "soul-heat" or heat belonging to the animating principle</note>.

And in the second book of *On the Generation of Animals*, chapter 3:

> <note>original Greek: πάντων μὲν γὰρ ἐν τῷ σπέρματι ἐνυπάρχει, ὅπερ ποιῆ γόνιμα εἶναι τὰ σπέρματα, τοῦτο δ’ οὐ πῦρ οὐδὲ τοιαύτη δύναμίς ἐστιν ἀλλὰ τὸ ἐμπεριλαμβανόμενον ἐν τῷ σπέρματι, καὶ ἐν τῷ ἀφρώδει πνεῦμα, καὶ ἡ ἐν τῷ πνεύματι φύσις, ἀνάλογος οὖσα τῷ τῶν ἄστρων στοιχείῳ.</note> 
> For in the semen of all things there is present that which makes the seeds fertile; and this is not fire, nor any such power, but the **spirit** <note>*pneuma*</note> contained within the semen and the frothy matter, and the nature within that spirit is analogous to the element of the stars.

The **spirit** <note>original: *pneuma*</note> cannot be elementary, because it is devoid of elementary properties, and its works are more divine than any that would suggest a purely elementary origin. Therefore, it is celestial and a **fifth essence** <note>original: *quintum*; the "quintessence," a substance distinct from the four earthly elements</note> apart from the four elements, left behind by the action of the celestial bodies upon the mixed and passive elementary world.
